source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម) - "ដំណាំក្រូចពោធិសាត់" (Pursat Orange Cultivation Guide), 2016, 26pp
text:
Pursat orange (ក្រូចពោធិសាត់) is one of Cambodia's best-known citrus fruits, named after Pursat province where it has traditionally been grown. Farmers and consumers across the country value it as a fresh-eating fruit and as a household source of vitamin C.

Citrus fruits in general are an important source of vitamin C for the body. According to the source, about 100 grams of Pursat orange juice can supply roughly one day's vitamin C requirement for a person, taken from around 7-8 segments (ភាគ) of fruit. Sweet orange varieties (ក្រូចឡើង) are also rich in vitamin C, and lime (ក្រូចឆ្មារ) is commonly used as a cooking condiment because its sour juice improves the flavor of many Khmer dishes, even though it is not eaten as a standalone fruit the way Pursat orange is.

Because of this nutritional value and its recognizable local identity, Pursat orange is grown both for home consumption and as a cash crop, with fresh fruit sold in local markets and, when supply is large, transported to markets in other provinces.
